title: Best Help Desk Software for Small Business
summary: Find the best help desk software for small businesses, with features, pricing, and tools to simplify ticket management and customer support.
body_markdown:
Small businesses handle a growing volume of support requests across multiple channels, from customer inquiries and IT tickets to HR questions and internal operations. The challenge is not whether requests will come in. The challenge is whether the team can respond fast enough to meet expectations while keeping everything organized.


For small businesses without large support teams, managing requests through shared email inboxes or informal Slack threads can make it difficult to maintain timely responses. A dedicated help desk gives small teams the structure to track requests, automate repetitive work, and scale support without adding headcount.


For teams that already work in Slack, a[Slack-native help desk](https://unthread.io/products/slack-support/?ref=unthread.io) like Unthread can turn channels such as #it-help or #support into fully structured internal help desks with ticket tracking, SLA management, and purpose-built AI agents built in.


## **Key Takeaways**


- Small businesses should prioritize help desk software that supports multi-channel intake, ticket routing, workflow automation, knowledge base management, and reporting.
- Unthread is the recommended option for teams that work in Slack and want[purpose-built AI agents](https://unthread.io/products/agentic-ai?ref=unthread.io) across IT, HR, and internal operations.
- The best help desk setup reduces manual triage while keeping the employee experience simple through[Slack-native ticketing](https://unthread.io/products/slack-support?ref=unthread.io) and automated workflows.
- Small businesses should evaluate pricing and plan features carefully, including AI automation availability, integration capabilities, and potential costs as support needs grow.
- Unthread's[self-learning knowledge base](https://unthread.io/products/agentic-ai?ref=unthread.io) helps teams identify documentation gaps and generate draft articles from resolved support conversations.


## **What Small Businesses Should Look for in Help Desk Software**


Small business support has different requirements than enterprise service management. A five-person team cannot dedicate full-time administrators to a complex platform. At the same time, growing businesses need more than a shared inbox to keep requests from falling through the cracks.


A strong help desk tool for small businesses should help teams:


- Convert emails, Slack messages, chat, and other channels into trackable tickets
- Route requests by topic, urgency, or team member availability
- Automate recurring Tier 1 questions and routine workflows
- Build a reusable[knowledge base](https://unthread.io/products/knowledge-base/?ref=unthread.io) from resolved requests
- Track SLAs, response times, and resolution metrics
- Connect with CRM, HRIS, and business tools through relevant[integrations](https://unthread.io/products/integrations/?ref=unthread.io)


The most practical systems let small teams keep everyday request intake simple while adding structure behind the scenes.

## **2) Help Scout**


Help Scout is an email-first help desk platform that emphasizes simplicity and a conversational support experience.


### **Where It Fits**


Help Scout is relevant for small businesses that handle most support through email and want a shared inbox that feels less like a corporate ticketing system. It is particularly useful for teams transitioning from Gmail or Outlook-based support.


### **Key Capabilities**


- Shared inbox with collaborative features and collision detection
- AI Answers and AI Drafts for automated responses
- Built-in knowledge base (Docs) and live chat widget (Beacon)
- Free plan for up to 5 users with 100 contacts per month
- Paid plans starting at $25/user/month


### **What Small Businesses Should Review**


Help Scout works well for email-centric teams. Small businesses that want Slack-native intake, purpose-built AI agents for triage, or cross-functional routing may need broader capabilities.


## **3) Zendesk**


Zendesk is an established help desk software platform, serving over 80,000 businesses worldwide.


### **Where It Fits**


Zendesk is relevant for small businesses planning significant growth or those that need omnichannel support across email, chat, phone, and social from day one. It offers a path from small business to enterprise scale.


### **Key Capabilities**


- Omnichannel ticketing across email, chat, phone, social, and messaging
- AI agents included in all plans with usage limits
- Marketplace with 1,800+ integrations
- Support Team plan starting at $19/agent/month
- AI Copilot available at $50/agent/month


### **What Small Businesses Should Review**


Zendesk offers a broad range of support features and configuration options. Small teams should evaluate its pricing, implementation requirements, and available capabilities based on their support needs.


## **4) Jira Service Management**


Jira Service Management is Atlassian's ITIL-aligned service desk, designed for IT teams managing internal requests.


### **Where It Fits**


Jira Service Management is most relevant for technical teams handling IT service requests, incident management, and change management. The free tier supports up to 3 agents.


### **Key Capabilities**


- Incident, problem, change, and release management workflows
- Native integration with Jira Software for development teams
- Self-service portal with Confluence knowledge base
- Free plan for up to 3 agents
- Standard plan at approximately $23/agent/month for 10 agents


### **What Small Businesses Should Review**


The fit is clearer for teams already using Atlassian tools. Non-technical small businesses may find the platform more complex than necessary for general support.


## **5) Freshdesk**


Freshdesk is Freshworks' help desk platform, often considered an alternative to Zendesk for growing teams.


### **Where It Fits**


Freshdesk offers help desk functionality for growing teams, including automation, AI capabilities, and tiered pricing options.


### **Key Capabilities**


- Omnichannel ticketing with email, chat, phone, and social support
- Freddy AI Agent with 500 sessions included
- Freddy AI Copilot available
- Growth plan starting at $19/agent/month
- Free plan for 1-2 agents for 6 months


### **What Small Businesses Should Review**


Freshdesk supports growing teams with automation and omnichannel features. Small businesses should evaluate its available plans based on their support requirements and expected ticket volume.


## **6) Zoho Desk**


Zoho Desk offers a low-cost paid tier starting at $7/user/month while still including AI features.


### **Where It Fits**


Zoho Desk offers help desk functionality for budget-conscious small businesses, with a free plan supporting up to 3 users.


### **Key Capabilities**


- Multi-channel ticketing system with email, chat, social, and phone
- Zia AI assistant included on all plans, including free
- Community forums feature
- Express plan at $7/user/month, Standard at $14/user/month
- Deep integration with Zoho CRM, Books, and Projects


### **What Small Businesses Should Review**


Zoho Desk offers tiered pricing and integrations with other Zoho products, including Zoho CRM, Books, and Projects.


## **7) HubSpot Service Hub**


HubSpot Service Hub connects help desk functionality with the broader HubSpot ecosystem for sales, marketing, and service alignment.


### **Where It Fits**


HubSpot Service Hub is most relevant for small businesses already using HubSpot CRM. The integration eliminates data silos between customer support and sales/marketing operations.


### **Key Capabilities**


- Unified help desk connected to HubSpot CRM database
- Skill-based automatic ticket assignment
- AI features using HubSpot Credits (monthly allowance included)
- Free plan for up to 2 users
- Starter plan at $7/seat/month, Professional at $90/seat/month


### **What Small Businesses Should Review**


The value proposition is strongest for existing HubSpot users. Teams not already in the HubSpot ecosystem may find standalone help desk tools more practical.


## **8) Hiver**


Hiver runs directly inside Gmail, providing a familiar interface for teams that primarily use Google Workspace.


### **Where It Fits**


Hiver is relevant for small businesses that want help desk functionality without leaving Gmail. The interface is immediately familiar to anyone who uses email.


### **Key Capabilities**


- Shared inbox with collision alerts and assignment running inside Gmail
- AI Agents included on every plan
- Collaboration features including comments, assignments, and shared drafts
- Free plan available
- Growth plan at $25/user/month, Pro at $55/user/month


### **What Small Businesses Should Review**


Hiver works well for Gmail-centric teams. Businesses that use Slack as their primary workspace may prefer a Slack-native tool for better workflow alignment.


## **9) Intercom**


Intercom is a chat-first platform designed for real-time customer conversations and proactive engagement.


### **Where It Fits**


Intercom is relevant for SaaS companies and digital businesses where live chat is the primary support channel. It combines support with product tours and in-app messaging.


### **Key Capabilities**


- Live chat and messaging as the primary channel
- Fin AI bot for automated resolutions
- Product tours and in-app messaging capabilities
- Essential plan at $19/seat/month plus AI usage
- Advanced plan at $85/seat/month


### **What Small Businesses Should Review**


Intercom's AI pricing is usage-based and can vary based on ticket volume. Small businesses should model total costs based on expected resolution volume.


## **10) Front**


Front is a shared inbox platform built for teams that prioritize internal collaboration on customer communications.


### **Where It Fits**


Front is relevant for operations teams that need collaborative features like internal comments, shared drafts, and assignment workflows within a shared inbox model.


### **Key Capabilities**


- Shared inbox with internal comments and drafts
- Autopilot AI for automated workflows
- Omnichannel support starting at Professional tier
- Starter plan at $25/seat/month
- Professional plan at $65/seat/month


### **What Small Businesses Should Review**


Front emphasizes collaboration over traditional ticketing. Teams that need structured ticket management and SLA tracking may prefer dedicated help desk platforms.

## **Frequently Asked Questions**


### **What are the core benefits of help desk software for a small business?**


Help desk software helps small businesses convert scattered requests into trackable tickets with ownership, routing, and status management. This matters because informal email threads and Slack DMs make it difficult to track response times or ensure nothing falls through the cracks.


A dedicated[Slack-native help desk](https://unthread.io/products/slack-support/?ref=unthread.io) provides the structure needed to scale support without adding headcount. The right platform automates repetitive work and keeps requests organized as the team grows.


### **How can AI help my small business's customer support?**


AI can help answer routine questions, route tickets to the right team members, and automate repetitive workflows.[Purpose-built AI agents](https://unthread.io/products/agentic-ai/?ref=unthread.io) work with internal knowledge and ticket context to reduce manual triage while escalating complex matters to the right staff.


Teams using AI help desks report significant time savings on Tier 1 requests. Effective systems combine automation with human oversight for consistent support.


### **Is it possible to manage both external customer support and internal IT/HR requests with one help desk solution?**


Yes, platforms like Unthread support both external customer support and internal[employee support](https://unthread.io/solutions/employee-support/?ref=unthread.io) across IT, HR, finance, and operations. A single platform can handle different queues with separate routing rules, SLAs, and privacy settings for each team.


This approach reduces the need for multiple tools while maintaining appropriate access controls. Unified platforms reduce tool sprawl and simplify support operations.


### **How important is a self-learning knowledge base for small businesses?**


A[self-learning knowledge base](https://unthread.io/products/knowledge-base/?ref=unthread.io) reduces the time spent answering repeated questions. Instead of manually creating documentation, the system identifies common questions from resolved tickets and drafts help articles for team review.


This approach helps small teams build useful documentation without dedicating significant time to content creation. Over time, the knowledge base helps resolve routine questions and empowers users to find answers independently.
